subject: law

source.document: A-level Law Specification — version 1.1, July 2026 (for A-level exams June 2019 onwards)
source.track: A Level · ages 16–19 · linear two-year course · Paper 1 Criminal law, Paper 2 Tort, Paper 3 Law of contract or Human rights — the nature of law and the English legal system is assessed in all three papers

note: Units follow the specification's numbered subject content (3.1–3.5). Content 3.1–3.3 is core; Law of contract and Human Rights are the two Paper 3 options and the atlas tracks both. The advanced and expert lessons extend the specification's English doctrine into jurisprudence and comparative systems.

program.title: The nature of law and the English legal system
topics: Nature of law: law and society
Nature of law: law and morality
Nature of law: law and justice
The legal system: the civil courts and other forms of dispute resolution
The legal system: the criminal courts and lay people
The legal system: legal personnel and the judiciary
The legal system: access to justice and funding

program.title: Criminal law
topics: Defences — capacity defences: insanity, automatism, intoxication
Defences — necessity defences: self-defence/prevention of crime, duress

program.title: Tort
topics: Liability in negligence for physical injury to people and damage to property
Liability in negligence for economic loss and psychiatric injury
Nuisance and the escape of dangerous things

program.title: Law of contract
topics: Contract terms: specific terms implied by statute law in relation to consumer contracts

program.title: Human Rights
topics: Human Rights in the United Kingdom prior to the Human Rights Act 1998
Human Rights in the United Kingdom after the enactment of the Human Rights Act 1998
The European Convention on Human Rights 1953: Articles 2, 5, 8, 10 and 11
